title: Streamed soundtrack and a Jukebox player
summary: All 21 original songs now stream as AAC through one media element (ranged reads, native decoding, seekable) instead of being decoded from 1 MiB VAG chunks in WebAssembly. A new Jukebox in the Main Menu and Pause uses the original Jukebox page art: the red snow backdrop and the spinning CD from PAGE14.RES.
details: The packager decodes each VAG with the same Rust stream decoder and encodes deterministic AAC-LC 160 kbps: 87.4 MB for the soundtrack instead of 218.4 MB. The Rust catalog and shuffle still choose every song. The Worker serves /content/<sha256>.m4a as audio/mp4 with byte ranges. Any missing stream or playback failure falls back to the original VAG decoder.

The Jukebox has genre, title and artist from music.pb, a seek bar, previous/play-pause/next, volume, a spectrum and all 21 songs, with keyboard and controller navigation. The disc ships no album covers, so the original CD and backdrop are the artwork.

Host Chromium: tools/test_jukebox.mjs passes Main and Pause Jukebox with 206 audio/mp4 range responses, selection, seeking, pause and resume, next and previous, and 390x844 touch sizes. test_music (decoder fallback), test_pause_menu, test_frontend and test_touch pass. Against the previously published package it plays through the decoder without errors.
limitation: AAC is an authored re-encoding of the decoded ADPCM, not an original file. Physical iOS and Android playback is unverified. The layout, transport and spectrum are authored, not a recovered native Jukebox.
